analysis.evidence: In לֹא יִירָשְׁךָ זֶה, “this man will not inherit from you,” זֶה refers back to the household member Abram mentioned in verse 3. The rest of verse 4 identifies Abram’s own offspring as his heir.

analysis.evidence: The clause אֲשֶׁר יֵצֵא מִמֵּעֶיךָ identifies the heir as one who will come forth from Abram’s own body. This distinguishes his offspring from זֶה, the man Abram had expected to inherit.
analysis.morphology: The preposition מִן means ‘from’. Its final נ assimilates to the initial מ of the masculine plural construct noun, producing the dagesh. The second-person masculine singular suffix ךָ means ‘your’ and refers to Abram.
analysis.sense: Inward parts, here referring to Abram’s own body as the source of his offspring.

analysis.evidence: הוּא resumes אֲשֶׁר יֵצֵא מִמֵּעֶיךָ, “the one who will come from your own body,” as the subject of יִירָשֶׁךָ, “will inherit from you.” The contrast with זֶה, “this one,” emphasizes which person will inherit.
analysis.morphology: Independent third-person masculine singular personal pronoun, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The verse repeats the verb with the same suffix. לֹא יִירָשְׁךָ זֶה rules out the man Abram had in mind. In the affirmative clause, הוּא points back to אֲשֶׁר יֵצֵא מִמֵּעֶיךָ and identifies Abram’s own offspring as his heir.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third-person masculine singular, with a second-person masculine singular object suffix referring to Abram.
